videos.title: Strength, Technique & CONDITIONING. The three essential components of a good armwrestler
videos.summary:
I put out a post on Instagram today about the three essential components of a good armwrestler: strength, technique and conditioning. Most people who train in this sport pour their time and energy into strength, and very little into the other two. Champions do all three, back to back, over and over again throughout their journey.

Strength will get you into the match. Technique will amplify the power you have. Conditioning will give you the resilience to survive this brutal sport. Strength alone very clearly isn't enough.

In this one we cover:
- Why armwrestling isn't as simple as powerlifting, and why technique has to come first
- The curse of strength: why already-strong beginners are often the hardest to teach
- The advice Devon gave me in 2014, and why Chetna is the one teaching me strength
- What conditioning actually is: your body's resilience to the stresses of this sport
- Why side pressure isn't a natural movement, and where that "magical" force that wins centre comes from
- Why two pullers of the same strength are not equal, and how to rest your muscles on your joints
- Devon's endurance: position, fuel management, and the five-second rule
- How to beat someone who is genuinely stronger than you
- Why people can still pull at a high level into their 60s
- How I build it: lean on your elbow every day, 5 to 15 kilos, for 15 minutes

videos.title: What Devon is Missing Regarding Side Pressure
videos.summary:
Devon recently shared a reel on side pressure: after countless elbow surgeries, his advice is don't go hard directly sideways, bring people this way instead. I'm glad I made the B-roll in it, right after Todd Hutchings. Devon taught me a lot when he came to Australia in 2014, and he's right that hand control can feel like side pressure to your opponent. But I think there's one thing he's missing here: static side pressure through the elbow.

In this one we cover:
- How supination and hand control convert to what feels like side pressure for your opponent
- What static side pressure is, and why you can't supinate or pronate your way into the centre before the go
- Winning the starting quadrant with a flat wrist and square shoulders
- The balance point where the hands stop changing and it comes down to pure side pressure
- A pro match where one puller won the hand control battle and still lost the match
- Why elite opponents don't fall apart when you take something off them
- Armwrestling as two battles: one to create opportunity, one to finish the match
- How I train it: heavy once a week and leaning on my elbow every single day

videos.title: King's Move: Who Gasses Out First? #armwrestling
videos.summary:
Janis Amolins on the worst scenario against a King's Move: you can't finish, so you just wait to see who gasses out first, and that lock doesn't get tired. Make him the one holding on instead. Full video with Janis is on the channel.
